title: Your First Weekend at CUNY Hunter College, Shared as Cards
description: Navigate the vertical campus and Upper East Side with this guide to your first weekend as a Hunter Hawk.

cards.title: Check In for Orientation
cards.subtitle: 904 Lexington Avenue
cards.notes: Start your weekend by checking in at the corner of 68th and Lexington to receive your visitor pass and orientation materials.
cards.short_summary: The primary entry point for new students and guests to access the main 68th Street campus buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Guests must check in at the 68th Street Visitors Center at 904 Lexington Avenue to gain access to campus locations like the cafeteria and student center.
cards.access_notes: Located at the corner of 68th Street and Lexington Avenue.

cards.title: Navigate the Sky Bridges
cards.subtitle: Connecting East, West, and North Buildings
cards.notes: Walk between buildings without hitting the street; the 3rd and 7th floor bridges offer great views of the city skyline.
cards.short_summary: Elevated glass walkways that connect the main campus buildings, essential for navigating the vertical campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Sky bridges connect the East and West buildings on floors 3 and 7, while North and West are connected on the 3rd floor.
cards.access_notes: Accessible to students with a valid Hunter OneCard; bridges are located on floors 3 and 7.

cards.title: Grab Lunch at the Cafeteria
cards.subtitle: West Building, 3rd Floor
cards.notes: Visit the main dining hub for halal-certified dishes, Italian-inspired hot meals, and a full salad bar.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus cafeteria offering diverse food stations including kosher and halal options.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hungry Hawk cafeteria on the third floor features Italian and Spanish-inspired dishes, a dedicated halal station, and grab-and-go kosher meals.
cards.source_title: Hunter Campus To Feature New World of Food Offerings
cards.access_notes: Open during standard campus hours; located on the 3rd floor of the West Building.

cards.title: Find Your Study Spot
cards.subtitle: East Building
cards.notes: Explore the newly renovated 5th floor to find group study rooms equipped with wireless display monitors.
cards.short_summary: The main campus library providing extensive study spaces, technology loans, and research support.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cooperman Library offers reservable group study rooms on the 5th floor equipped with display monitors for student use.
cards.access_notes: Open 8:30am – 8:00pm on weekdays; requires Hunter OneCard for entry.

cards.title: Take a Break in the Park
cards.subtitle: Entrance at 5th Avenue and 68th Street
cards.notes: Walk two blocks west to reach the park; the Conservatory Water area is perfect for watching model boats.
cards.short_summary: A massive urban park located just steps from the Hunter campus, offering a natural escape for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Hunter College is conveniently walking distance from Central Park, which offers free activities like watching model boats at Conservatory Water.
cards.access_notes: Public park open daily from 6:00am to 1:00am.

cards.title: Meet Peers at the Game Room
cards.subtitle: Thomas Hunter Hall, Room 205
cards.notes: Join Welcome Week events like the Ice Cream Social or Games & Grub to connect with fellow Hawks.
cards.short_summary: A social hub in Thomas Hunter Hall used for student government events and casual recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Game Room in Thomas Hunter Hall, Room 205, hosts Welcome Week events like 'Games & Grub' and 'Ice Cream Socials'.
cards.access_notes: Located on the 2nd floor of Thomas Hunter Hall; check the student activities calendar for event times.

cards.title: Explore Campus Art
cards.subtitle: West Building Entrance
cards.notes: Visit this gallery to see historical and scholarly exhibitions; it is one of the few campus spaces open to the public.
cards.short_summary: The main campus art gallery featuring rotating exhibitions and BFA degree shows.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bertha and Karl Leubsdorf Gallery is located on the main campus and can be accessed directly through the West Building's entrance.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public during gallery hours; enter via the West Building.

cards.title: Visit the Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: West Building, B2 Level
cards.notes: Check out the weightlifting facilities and open gym areas to plan your workout routine for the semester.
cards.short_summary: The primary recreation facility for students, offering fitness classes and gym equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fitness Center is located on the B2 Level in the West Building of the Hunter College 68th Street Campus.
cards.access_notes: Requires a valid Hunter OneCard and a completed fitness waiver for entry.

cards.title: Order Your Textbooks
cards.subtitle: Digital Platform
cards.notes: Use the online portal to compare prices and rent or buy your required course materials before classes start.
cards.short_summary: The official platform for Hunter students to acquire textbooks and academic supplies.
cards.evidence_claim: Students can purchase or rent books and course materials from the online Hunter College Online Bookstore.
cards.access_notes: Accessible 24/7 online; physical pickup locations may vary by semester.

cards.title: Master the Commute
cards.subtitle: Lexington Avenue and 68th Street
cards.notes: Locate the direct campus entrance from the 6 train station to save time on your first day of classes.
cards.short_summary: The primary subway station serving the college, featuring a direct entrance into the North Building.
cards.evidence_claim: The main campus is accessible from the 68th Street - Hunter College stop on the MTA's 6 train.
cards.access_notes: Direct entrance to the North Building is available from the subway platform.
